answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: No, please skip the 16-miler. A long run six days out would not add fitness, it would only cost you leg freshness on race day; the 20-miler on Oct 4 and the 17-miler on Sep 27 are the runs that will carry you. Heavy, flat legs right now are the classic taper feeling, not a loss of form, and the sharpness returns in the last few days. Hold the line and show up fresh.

new.analysis:
## How last week went
You executed the first taper week cleanly: five runs, 34 miles, the 8-miler with marathon-pace miles right on target around 8:34/mi, and the 12-mile long run steady at 10:00/mi with only a 7 bpm drift. Nothing was skipped, nothing was overrun, and no pain anywhere. That is exactly what a taper week is supposed to look like.

## Why the legs feel flat
A sharp cut in volume lets accumulated fatigue surface before the freshness arrives, and the heavy, dead feeling you are describing lines up with that. Your easy pace and heart rate have been flat at 9:51/mi and 139 bpm for a month, which is a sign the engine is intact, not fading.

## Shape of race week
This week has one job: arrive on the start line rested and ready. The plan keeps mileage low, drops in a very short marathon-pace touch on Wed so race pace feels familiar, and finishes with a tiny shakeout on Saturday with a few strides to wake the legs up. Target pace for sub-3:45 is 8:34/mi; on race day settle into the first 5 miles no faster than 8:40/mi, then let it come to you.

## Logistics worth sorting now
Lay out kit, bib and gels by Thursday, start topping up carbs from Friday, and avoid anything new on Saturday night. If anything feels off in the body during the week, back off rather than push through, and send me a note.
